author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Syria’s plan to convert the former Mezzeh military airport in Damascus into a private-jet hub is drawing warnings from rights groups and nearby residents. They say construction could disturb suspected mass graves and forensic evidence while moving ahead of unresolved claims over land taken from local families decades ago.

Documents reviewed by Reuters indicate that the site was used for detention and executions under Bashar al-Assad’s government. The Syria Justice and Accountability Centre says its records point to graves containing more than 1,150 detainees who died after torture or execution. Preserving those locations could be essential to identifying victims and documenting abuses.

Residents of nearby Moadamiya also say land was expropriated for the military airport in the 1950s without compensation. They have protested and asked for a role in decisions about the redevelopment, including a process for ownership and compensation claims. United Nations officials have called on Syria to address property rights, but authorities had not provided substantive public safeguards for either the suspected graves or the disputed land. The project therefore remains under active scrutiny.
dek: Rights groups and residents say converting the former Mezzeh military airport into a private-jet hub could disturb evidence and unresolved property claims.
headline: Damascus airport plan raises mass-grave and land-rights alarm
